I keep seeing I2p suggested here. Have you tried it?

I was just playing around with it earlier today, actually. Tried it out years ago, but it was a wasteland. It still more-or-less is, but it has more activity than it used to. It's a nice little place to curiously poke around, and there's an email system that can send/receive mail from the clear-web, which is neat. A few torrent sites (which, surprisingly, have lots of decently seeded files), Newsgroups, and even a built-in i2p version of KaZaA/Gnutella.

It'll probably pick up steam as the clear-web becomes more heavily regulated, especially now that Cloudflare and the like are censoring. So you'd might as well familiarize yourself with it sooner rather than later.

I will say, I just tried out ZeroNet today, and the barrier of entry is MUCH lower. You can direct all your traffic to/from it through Tor, and lots of people are doing crazy things, integrating it with IPFS (among other techs) to make totally viable (and 100% decentralized) sites. There's anonymous social networking (fb, twitter clones, etc), torrent sites, chans (active ones, too! I couldn't believe it), forums, blogs, a "Daily Stormer" mirror, HTML5 games, huge book libraries, etc. Someone's even working on (apparently) a Voat clone.

If you're not familiar with ZeroNet, it's a decentralized internet that runs on torrent-like tech. You can register domains with Namecoin (decentralized/Blockchain DNS), and it's easy af to get running. You only contribute files to the network that you're trying to/have viewed, or you can choose to download all the files for a site and support it by seeding it from your PC. The more people use it, the faster everything works, too.

The only downside is that it's nowhere near as anonymous as other networks (yet), but it's incredibly robust for a project in its infancy. Definitely only use it by forcing connections through Tor and loading it through Tor Browser— simply for the sake of giving it that little extra boost in network-traffic obfuscation. All other standard OpSec rules apply. Also, JavaScript everywhere. You definitely need it enabled for everything to work, so just remember that.
